newsitem.title: TAIWAN: BASEBALL-TAIWAN LEAGUE URGES LEGALISED GAMBLING.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TAIWAN LEAGUE URGES LEGALISED GAMBLING.

text.p: Taiwan's professional baseball league, under investigation for gambling and game-fixing, urged the government on Tuesday to legalise sports betting -- saying it would prevent organised crime from manipulating game results.

"We must have a clear separation between betting on the games and the games themselves. We must not let gambling interfere with game results," Chinese Professional Baseball League secretary-general Daniel Tu said in a statement issued by a league official.
"One way we can ensure such a separation is for the government to legalise gambling," Tu said.

Taiwan bans all gambling, but several senior officials -- including Vice-President Lien Chan -- have urged legalisation, arguing that authorities would be able to better scrutinise betting and spot irregularities and that legal gambling would induce would-be illegal bettors to do it legally.

The legitimacy of Taiwan's seven-year-old baseball league suffered a major blow recently with prosecutors' allegations that many of its players and coaches threw games in return for huge kickbacks from gangsters during the 1996 season.
In January, five players were arrested for suspected involvement in game-fixing and investigators said more arrests were possible.
After the 1996 season, the league asked Taiwan's Justice Ministry to investigate 13 games in which league officials suspected "irregular" on-field activities.
The baseball crackdown is part of a continuing Justice Ministry campaign to purge the country of the widespread influence of gangsters.
